data: © JAXA — Smart Lander for Investigating Moon. Landed tilted; intermittent operations as solar panels rotate into sunlight.
小型月着陸実証機 SLIM (ISAS/JAXA)

Japan's Smart Lander demonstrated pinpoint precision landing — targeting within 100 m accuracy vs the km-scale standard of all previous missions. Landed nose-down at roughly 90° from the intended attitude, leaving its solar panels initially pointing away from the Sun; operations resumed nine days later once the Sun angle shifted. Japan became the fifth nation to achieve a lunar soft landing.

Pinpoint landing accuracy — bridges the gap between 'we can land somewhere on this body' and 'we can land at the specific scientifically valuable rock', the precondition for surface-asset rendezvous on Mars.

SLIM (Smart Lander for Investigating Moon) landed in Shioli Crater on January 20, 2024 — Japan's first soft landing on the Moon and a precision-landing technology demonstrator. SLIM touched down within 100 m of its target (the previous best was 1+ km), but flipped onto its side and operated upside-down on its remaining solar cells until power ran out. Two surface micro-rovers, LEV-1 and LEV-2 (Sora-Q), deployed before the awkward final orientation.
SLIM lander pre-launch — 200 kg, pencil-shaped, designed for low-mass precision landing demos.
LEV-2 "Sora-Q" — a baseball-sized transformer ball-rover developed by TOMY (the toy company) + JAXA + Sony.
H-IIA-47 lifts off carrying SLIM + XRISM observatory — a co-launch with a major X-ray science mission.
SLIM photographed by Sora-Q on the lunar surface — landed nose-down, solar panels facing the wrong way.
Despite the unintended orientation, SLIM operated three times — at lunar sunrise it caught angled sun on its inverted-facing panels and woke up briefly.
